title: arngz finds each op's window through hs.window.get, which re-reads every app through Accessibility
body:
arngz's engine finds a window by `hs.window.get(id)` once per op (arngz.lua:755, 974, 1107 and 2223 at cc/desks1126 79cb2c79). In Hammerspoon 1.1.1, `hs.window.get` is `window.find`, which calls `window.allWindows()` each time (extensions/hs/window.lua:203-236). That reads every running app's windows through Accessibility, on Hammerspoon's main thread.

The cost: each op waits on every app, the slow ones too. On 26 Nov 2026 zeopit had six apps whose windows Accessibility cannot name. hv's apply (run 20261126T080529Z-88063) did 7 ops in 51 s, so the cost is bounded there. But one app whose Accessibility never answers blocks the op, and with it Hammerspoon. A diagnostic that called `hs.window.get` once per window id (cc's sysids r1) left Hammerspoon unresponsive until hv restarted it. `hs -t` stops only the client, and every later call queues behind the Lua that still runs.

The fix: look the window up in observe's index first (one `allWindows` per run, which `index_windows` already reads at arngz.lua:264), and call `hs.window.get` only for an id that is not there. Size S.

Tests: engine_test, with the fake hs. (1) An op on a window in the index makes no `hs.window.get` call. (2) An op on a window not in the index calls it once. (3) The window that each op acts on is the index's. Each arm is red over the current code.



hv decision 49 (26 Nov 2026, through vc): this fix goes into 2.15.0. Its design is in cc's note desks1125/a-fixes-note.md, part 2.
